surprise: Every run whose gate passes halts while relaying regeneration-cycle/gate-attempt-passed to measurement: halt detail "measurement: regeneration-cycle/gate-attempt-passed: class java.time.Instant cannot be cast to class java.util.Date". The event is never handed in (measurement's store has no gate-attempt-passed). Regeneration-cycle's store keeps passed-at as a grain/instant (java.time.Instant), while specification's and cycle-preparation's instants (relayed fine) are java.util.Date. Handing the same event to the gated measurement candidate directly, passed-at as ISO text, is accepted (transcript/probe-meas-direct-handin/response.json). So no run can reach awaiting-verdicts with the real gated candidates; every verdict, score and scoreboard item is unreachable. The halt is also labelled context-did-not-respond, though the context was never asked.

With the port held, regeneration-cycle refuses the runner's record-gate-attempt with reason-does-not-fit-outcome, and record-gate-refusal is refused with no refusal code. The runner retried 11 times at the same attempt (positions 9 to 30), then halted {effect gate-refusal, reason effect-could-not-run, detail "Gate refusals did not conclude the cycle"}.

Host load, not the candidate: the machine ran at load 40-55 (a long-running VM and other processes). The five gated JVM contexts often took over 30 s to boot together, and the runner refused contexts-not-responding naming all five (also 06-050, which checks contexts before the image). For that reason I named wrappers in LOYLY_CONTEXTS (grading/ctx/*.sh: the unchanged gated candidates with JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS='-XX:TieredStopAtLevel=1 -XX:ActiveProcessorCount=2 -XX:+UseSerialGC'), added one runs-to-advance read before each scenario, and reran any scenario that got an unexpected contexts-not-responding (s/done.txt, s/flaky/). The runner's own work before it starts the contexts (~30 s on the loaded host in 050's failed tries) seems to count toward that wait. The seam names no deadline.

Even though both runs halted, R-2 on the same LOYLY_MEASUREMENT_STORE relayed only that run's new handoffs, with positions counted from 1 (scenario-stamped #1, #2, source-cut-pinned #1), and H kept both runs' events. So the history-store relay window works up to the gate.

When the store-check command cannot be started, the identity probe (which launches start.sh) still ran before the halt (t045/probe-run.*.txt). The seam allows this, but the check could fail before booting anything.
After R-1 halted, start R-2 C-2 was accepted. In an earlier try on the loaded host it was refused contexts-not-responding naming cycle-preparation only.

Without BUILDER_IMAGE (t049b), the builder got two arguments, as before. With it, the image digest in the detail matches the candidate-digest formula over the image folder that I computed myself (sha256:07f0b66e...).
